issue_context.title: Failing LL.TS Data Length Update Tests (split)
issue_context.body:
**Description**
Failing LL.TS EBQ Tests for Data Length Update:
```
LL/CON/MAS/BV-74-C:
Master Data Length Update - Initiating Data Length Update Procedure; LE 1M PHY

LL/CON/MAS/BV-77-C:
Master Data Length Update - Initiating Data Length Update Procedure; LE 2M PHY

LL/CON/SLA/BV-131-C: 
Data Length Update - Retransmission During an Update

LL/CON/SLA/BV-78-C
Slave Data Length Update - Initiating Data Length Update Procedure; LE 1M PHY

LL/CON/SLA/BV-81-C:
Slave Data Length Update - Initiating Data Length Update Procedure; LE 2M PHY
```
**To Reproduce**
Run the listed LL.TS tests with EBQ and nRF52

**Expected behavior**
Tests should pass

**Impact**
Currently no practical impact, but qualification will fail
comments:
Only one DLE test case left failing on our side:
```
LL/CON/SLA/BV-131-C: 
Data Length Update - Retransmission During an Update
```
Note that feedback from Ellisys is that LL/CON/SLA/BV-131-C is an EBQ related issue, and not a problem in the  LL code

review_comments: delete lines 4538-4540. Move line 4531 after 4534. This is how its in legacy controller (keep your change in line 4534).
I will do so, but first I'll push an update which should work OK in Denmark; hopefully they can test while I rewrite the code as per your suggestion.
revert the MAX here as its applied in line 3233

Almost, here we calculate the time required for a packet when using coded phy
In line 3233 we apply the Bluetooth spec minimum requirement for rx-time (and tx-time)
there initializations are not needed if you have lines 3233 and 3234
They were added because the Clang compiler generated warnings/errors before the changes from this PR were added. No consequence for code-side, so I prefer to not remove this initialisation

use !! to convert to boolean and assign to u8_t

feature_coded_phy = !!(conn->llcp_feature.features & BIT(BT_LE_FEAT_BIT_PHY_CODED));

That does not give a reduction in code-size, and IMO does not increase readability. 
You still want me to make the change, given that code-size is unaltered?
revert the MAX here as its applied in line 3233

Almost, here we calculate the time required for a packet when using coded phy
In line 3233 we apply the Bluetooth spec minimum requirement for rx-time (and tx-time)
PKT_US(PDU_DC_PAYLOAD_SIZE_MIN, 0)  is 328, hence do not need to do MAX twice, waste of CPU time due to branching
There is no difference in code size either way; IMO as it is the code shows that there are 2 aspects in the length calculation; the compiler does its optimisation for reducing the code size
